subject: ela
skillName: Tell a story or recount an experience

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'I had a fun lunch.'
Description B: 'At lunch, I ate a peanut butter sandwich, an apple, and chocolate milk. My friend Tomás made me laugh so hard that milk came out of my nose.'

Which description gives more relevant details? Write A or B.

steps: Description A is very vague — it does not say what was eaten or what happened.
Description B names specific foods and includes a funny, specific moment.
The detail about milk coming out of his nose makes the scene real and memorable.
Description B gives a listener enough information to picture the lunch.

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'We planted seeds in the garden. We used small brown seeds. We dug little holes with our fingers, dropped in one seed each, covered them with soil, and watered them with a small red watering can.'
Description B: 'We did something in the garden. It was fun.'

Which description gives more relevant details? Write A or B.

steps: Description A describes the seeds, the process (digging holes with fingers), the action (one seed per hole), and the tool (red watering can).
Description B says nothing specific — it could describe almost any activity.
Relevant details tell the listener what, how, and with what.
Description A gives all three; Description B gives none.

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'My dog did something.'
Description B: 'My dog Pepper ran into the backyard, grabbed my sock off the clothesline, and buried it under the rose bush.'

Which description gives more relevant details? Write A or B.

steps: Description A tells the listener almost nothing — 'did something' could mean anything.
Description B names the dog (Pepper), describes what she did (grabbed a sock from the clothesline), and where she buried it (under the rose bush).
These specific details make the story funny and clear.
Description B answers: Who? What? Where?

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'We went on a walk and looked at things outside. Nature is pretty.'
Description B: 'On our nature walk, we spotted a red-tailed hawk sitting on a fence post, three yellow butterflies, and a turtle hiding under a log near the pond.'

Which description gives more relevant details? Write A or B.

steps: Description A says 'things outside' and 'nature is pretty' — these phrases mean nothing specific.
Description B names exactly what they saw: a hawk, butterflies, a turtle, and their locations.
These details paint a picture a listener can visualize.
Description B answers: What did you see? Where?

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'My birthday party was great. We had food and played games.'
Description B: 'At my birthday party, we played freeze dance in the living room and ate a chocolate cake shaped like a soccer ball. My friend Aisha fell over during freeze dance and everyone laughed, including her.'

Which description gives more relevant details? Write A or B.

steps: Description A uses 'food' and 'games' — too vague to picture.
Description B names the game (freeze dance), the location (living room), and the cake (chocolate, soccer ball shape).
The funny moment with Aisha adds a specific, memorable detail.
A listener can picture this party; they cannot picture Description A.

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'I saw something cool at the library. We went inside. There were books.'
Description B: 'At the library, I found a book about deep-sea creatures with glowing pictures on every page. I checked it out and read it twice before dinner.'

Which description gives more relevant details? Write A or B.

steps: Description A says 'something cool' and 'there were books' — unhelpful generalities.
Description B names the book's topic, describes the pictures (glowing), and tells what happened after (read it twice before dinner).
These details show what was exciting and personal about the visit.
A listener knows exactly why the library visit was interesting.

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'I helped my mom with dinner. We made something. It smelled good.'
Description B: 'I helped my mom make vegetable soup on a cold evening. I peeled the carrots and stirred the pot. The soup smelled like garlic and thyme, and it warmed me up from the inside.'

Which description gives more relevant details? Write A or B.

steps: Description A does not name what was made or what the student did.
Description B names the dish (vegetable soup), the time (cold evening), and the student's specific tasks (peeling carrots, stirring).
The smell is described with specific ingredients: garlic and thyme.
The ending detail ('warmed me up from the inside') shows how the experience felt.

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'Our teacher read a book to us. It was about animals. We liked it.'
Description B: 'Our teacher read Charlotte's Web to us after lunch every day for two weeks. My favorite part was when Wilbur found out Charlotte had written words in her web to save his life. Some kids cried.'

Which description gives more relevant details? Write A or B.

steps: Description A says 'a book about animals' — this describes thousands of books.
Description B names the book (Charlotte's Web), the schedule (after lunch, two weeks), and the most emotional moment.
The detail about some kids crying shows the impact of the book.
A listener who has not read the book can still understand why it mattered.

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'I got hurt once. It was bad. I felt better after.'
Description B: 'Last summer I fell off my bike on the gravel path in Riverside Park. I scraped both my knees and cried for a while. My dad cleaned the cuts, put on two bandages with smiley faces on them, and said I was the bravest kid in the park.'

Which description gives more relevant details? Write A or B.

steps: Description A says nothing specific: no location, no type of injury, no person helping.
Description B names when (last summer), where (Riverside Park), what happened (fell off bike on gravel), what was hurt (both knees), and how it was handled (bandages with smiley faces).
The dad's comment is a specific, warm, memorable detail.
A listener can picture the whole scene.

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'We did an experiment in science class. We mixed things together. It changed.'
Description B: 'In science class we mixed baking soda and vinegar in a plastic cup. The mixture hissed and bubbled up over the rim, and some of it spilled on Marcus's desk. He jumped back and everyone gasped.'

Which description gives more relevant details? Write A or B.

steps: Description A uses 'things' and 'changed' — hopelessly vague.
Description B names the ingredients (baking soda and vinegar), the container, and the exact reaction (hissed and bubbled).
The spill on Marcus's desk and the class reaction make the moment vivid and funny.
A listener can picture the scene and feel the excitement.

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'I visited my grandparents. We spent time together. It was nice.'
Description B: 'I spent last weekend at my grandparents' farm. My grandmother taught me how to collect eggs from the chickens, and I accidentally dropped one. My grandfather said every good farmer drops an egg now and then.'

Which description gives more relevant details? Write A or B.

steps: Description A gives no setting, no activity, no interaction.
Description B names the setting (farm), the activity (collecting eggs), the mistake (dropped one), and the grandfather's kind response.
The grandfather's comment is a specific, warm detail that shows his character.
A listener learns something real about the visit.

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'We saw fireworks. They were colorful. It was loud.'
Description B: 'On the Fourth of July, we sat on a blanket in the park and watched fireworks explode in red, gold, and purple bursts above the lake. The boom was so loud my little cousin covered her ears and buried her face in my mom's shoulder.'

Which description gives more relevant details? Write A or B.

steps: Description A says 'colorful' and 'loud' — every fireworks show is colorful and loud.
Description B names the holiday, the location (park near a lake), the specific colors (red, gold, purple), and the effect on a family member.
The cousin covering her ears and hiding is a specific, relatable detail.
It makes the scene feel real rather than generic.

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'I was nervous before something. Then it went okay.'
Description B: 'Before my spelling bee, my hands were shaking and I kept drinking water. When it was my turn, I spelled \"encyclopedia\" correctly, and my teacher jumped out of her chair.'

Which description gives more relevant details? Write A or B.

steps: Description A says 'something' and 'went okay' — no event, no outcome.
Description B names the event (spelling bee), describes physical nervousness (shaking hands, drinking water), and names the specific word spelled.
The teacher jumping out of her chair is a vivid, specific detail that shows the achievement.
A listener understands exactly what happened and how well the student did.

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'On the first day of school, I went to my classroom. I saw kids. My teacher said things.'
Description B: 'On my first day of second grade, I walked into Room 14 and saw my name on a desk next to a window. My teacher, Ms. Alvarez, had put a little welcome note under each pencil. Mine said: \"Welcome! I am so glad you are here.\"'

Which description gives more relevant details? Write A or B.

steps: Description A says 'saw kids' and 'said things' — no useful information.
Description B names the room (Room 14), the student's desk placement (by a window), the teacher (Ms. Alvarez), and quotes the welcome note.
The welcome note with its specific words makes the moment personal and warm.
A listener knows why this first day felt welcoming.

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'We made something in art. I worked hard. I was proud.'
Description B: 'In art class, I spent three days making a mosaic out of torn paper in shades of blue and green. It showed a fish swimming toward the light. My teacher displayed it in the front hallway, and my mom took a photo of it.'

Which description gives more relevant details? Write A or B.

steps: Description A says 'something in art' — no project, no process, no outcome.
Description B names the art form (mosaic), the materials (torn paper), the time spent (three days), the colors, the subject (fish), and the outcome (displayed in hallway).
The mom taking a photo is a final specific detail that shows how meaningful the artwork was.
A listener can picture both the artwork and the pride behind it.
